summary:
Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 9:

- Coach Kyle Shanahan is very close to being back at full speed. He came out to practice today at 10:26 am and was on the field for the whole thing. He's still not quite calling the offense and standing in his usual spot but he's getting there as evidenced by his surprise media session after practice. 

- The entire coaching staff was wearing Roger Craig No. 33 shirts in honor of the legendary running back as he goes into the Pro Football Hall of Fame today. 

- The only new name added to the list of non participants in practice on Saturday: LB Luke Gifford. It's unclear why he didn't participate but he did some work on the side. 

-  The full list of those missing practice today:  Gifford, OL Nick Zakelj (elbow), DE Nick Bosa (soreness), OL Carver Willis (concussion), WR Jacob Cowing (hip flexor strain), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (concussion), WR Christian Kirk (calf), WR Mike Evans (quad), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Kaelon Black (adductor), RB Jordan James (rib), DL Keion White (adductor), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle)    

Players on PUP: TE George Kittle (achilles), RB Isaac Guerendo (pec), DL Mykel Williams (ACL)

- Once again, many of these guys were doing some sort of work on the side. Evans looks close to full strength and Shanahan said Evans probably feels like he can be back now but they want to be smart with him.

- WR De'Zhaun Stribling and LB Dre Greenlaw were back in team drills in varying capacities after easing back in from a hamstring and soreness the other day. 

- Some notes from one-on-one pass rush drills: RG Dominick Puni looks like he's ready to take another big step forward and potentially set himself up for a nice pay day. He had excellent reps against DT Osa Odighizuwa and Gracen Halton. ... Colton McKivitz shut down DE Romello Height on the first rep of practice then did it again later. They ran it back and Height jumped offsides twice before finally getting past McKivitz with a nice spin move inside... Rough day for DT CJ West, who seemed to be struggling to keep his pads low. He came up out of his stance a bit high a few times and didn't generate much push on a few of his reps, including one where C Jake Brendel handled him well... Brendel also had a good rep against Sebastian Valdez... Rookie DTs James Thompson Jr. and Bryson Eason and Odighizuwa and got the better of Connor Colby... Drake Nugent had a couple of solid showings against Thompson and West... Still no Alfred Collins here, though he's been plenty involved in team periods. And no one-on-ones for Trent Williams today (though he usually only does one rep anyway). 

- Score one for the defense today, bouncing back after the top offense had torched it a couple of times during the week. 

- CB Upton Stout led the way with a couple of big plays. First, he had a diving pass breakup near the goal line on a pass from QB Brock Purdy intended for Demarcus Robinson. Later, Stout jumped a throw for Robinson, picked it off and returned it for a touchdown. Stout even did a front flip into the end zone to cap it off. 

- CB Deommodore Lenoir, who has had his share of pass breakups in this camp finally got his hands on one with another pick (and possible return for a TD?) on another throw from Purdy for Robinson. Seemed perhaps Purdy tried to squeeze some tight ones into Robinson and it just didn't work today like in recent practices.

- LB Fred Warner had an impressive pass breakup on a layered throw over the middle intended for Jordan Watkins. Warner also recovered what appeared to be a fumble early in the first period of team though it was unclear what exactly happened from my vantage point.

- DB Nate Hobbs flashed some play making today with a bit more work in team. He had a pair of pass breakups in the red zone, one on a throw for Watkins froM Mac Jones in the corner of the end zone (there was an offside penalty called here) and another on a throw over the middle from Adrian Martinez. 

- DT Gracen Halton had a nice run stuff against Patrick Taylor Jr. right before Stout's pick-6. Collins got his hand up and batted down a Kurtis Rourke pass. 

- The Niners did a lot of mixing and matching today on offense. There were times where the top OL worked with QB Kurtis Rourke and other QBs were in with different lines. Perhaps made things a bit more disjointed for the offense. 

- It wasn't all bad on that side of the ball, though. Had Purdy at 15-of-22, including a tight window TD in the red zone to TE Luke Farrell, who continues to be a favorite target for Purdy in this camp. Purdy also hit Farrell on a deep throw up the seam and hit WR Trenton Irwin on a deep ball early in practice as well as a nice job moving in the pocket and finding Christian McCaffrey for a big gain over the middle. 

- Stribling was back in the mix in team and making an impact again, catching balls from multiple quarterbacks on multiple routes for multiple sizable gains. Shanahan referred to Stribling picking things up in a hurry in his presser and it continues to look like -- if healthy -- Stribling could have a fairly extensive role early on. 

- The running back situation behind McCaffrey has no clarity right now because Black, James and Guerendo are out. Nothing against the others that are getting reps there but this is such a prime opportunity for one of those young backs to plant the flag as RB2 and it's just not happening because of injury. Perhaps some will return next week because the path is there.

-  The Niners are off tomorrow but we will have some access to assistant coaches. Will pass along some notables that come from that session and then right back to it next week with the Titans coming for joint practice on Tuesday and the preseason opener on Thursday. Thanks for reading.

summary:
Most competitive 49ers' training camp practice so far ended Block 3 — fittingly, it coincided with Kyle Shanahan's return to the podium. Some highlights:

🏈Upton Stout will be a HUGE part of this defense. Pick 6 on a Brock Purdy-to-Demarcus Robinson try today. Raheem Morris said Stout is SF's starting "Star" — that was Jalen Ramsey's versatile position in LA's defense
🏈OL/DL 1-on-1s didn't go well for Connor Colby, who lost multiple reps (rookie James Thompson got him twice). Robert Jones continued as top LG. Brett Toth (concussion) watched from sideline
🏈Romello Height had a fun multi-rep battle with Colton McKivitz. Slipped lost Round 1, then jumped offsides twice, then ripped out a wicked inside spin move — speedy potential on full display. Height says he picks Trent Williams' brain after practice (smart move, per sources)
🏈De'Zhaun Stribling was back in team drills. Purdy's first pass: Crisp out-breaker to the rookie, who continues to look polished and explosive. Stribling did log a catch vs Stout on another out later on
🏈Biggest offensive play came when 49ers spread defense out with Stribling and Co. to set up Purdy-to-McCaffrey on a 25-yard post 
🏈The logjam of young DTs — Sebastian Valdez, Bryson Eason, and James Thompson — will be interesting to sort out. All are flashing. Alfred Collins had a big pass bat-down today, one of his specialties
🏈Jordan Watkins has had some struggles over the middle and today he dropped an intermediate crosser in traffic from Adrian Martinez
🏈Nice adjustment from Junior Bergen on a similar route but with Kurtis Rourke at QB. Throw was a touch late and behind Bergen but the gritty young WR made it work. His good camp continues
🏈Best practice so far for vet CB Nate Hobbs, who notched 3 pass breakups, including one vs Bergen. Hobbs has been most effective inside during his career but he also knocked two boundary passes away today
🏈Soaring TD catch in end-of-game red-zone work from 6-2 rookie WR Wesley Grimes on a throw from Mac Jones
🏈Purdy found Luke Farrell for a last-second TD during his first turn of this hurry-up work. Farrell's pass-game usage has gone way up this camp; looks like a trusted target for 13 now
🏈Deommodore Lenoir INT of Purdy came on the first team's second red-zone try. Fourth down as time expired, so Purdy had to force a throw since no one was open and the "game" was on the line. Lenoir undercut Robinson
🏈Big run stop from rookie DT Gracen Halton, who's one of the most vocal players on the field. When Halton makes a play, you typically hear it from the sideline
🏈Fred Warner notched a lunging PBU, showcasing that rare 6-4 LB height, and also scooped up a possible early fumble for a return TD
🏈49ers will be off Sunday before returning for their fourth 2-practice block on Monday, the second of which will be a joint session with Robert Saleh and the Titans — so the work is ramping up at just the right time

title: Eagles Training Camp Player of the Day, Day 8: Darius Cooper I don’t there is a single player on offense who has improved more from last season than Darius Cooper. The best thing about Cooper is he is consistent. It feels like every day he makes a catch that stands out and Saturday was no different. Cooper had the catch of the day when he made a textbook impressive catch along the sideline. The pass was from Andy Dalton about 15 yards down the field. Cooper did an amazing job keeping his feet in bounds while his body fell out of bounds with his hands extended to make the catch. It reminded me of something Devonta Smith does routinely. Cooper now has 13 catches in training camp and it feels like the majority of them have been over 10 yards or longer. He hasn’t been getting check down targets. His targets are over the middle in tough coverage and he is consistently coming down with them. Cooper has not only earned a roster spot so far in camp but I think he has earned consistent playing time on offense.

Eagles Training Camp Player of the Day, Day 8: Darius Cooper

I don’t there is a single player on offense who has improved more from last season than Darius Cooper. 

The best thing about Cooper is he is consistent. It feels like every day he makes a catch that stands out and Saturday was no different. 

Cooper had the catch of the day when he made a textbook impressive catch along the sideline. The pass was from Andy Dalton about 15 yards down the field. Cooper did an amazing job keeping his feet in bounds while his body fell out of bounds with his hands extended to make the catch. It reminded me of something Devonta Smith does routinely. 

Cooper now has 13 catches in training camp and it feels like the majority of them have been over 10 yards or longer. He hasn’t been getting check down targets. His targets are over the middle in tough coverage and he is consistently coming down with them. 

Cooper has not only earned a roster spot so far in camp but I think he has earned consistent playing time on offense.

title: A quick Larry Fitzgerald story. When John McCain passed away in 2018 Larry was asked to speak at the service. McCain and Fitzgerald developed a unique friendship that dated back to 2006. They had a tremendous amount of respect for one another. Larry wanted that moment to be perfect. He considered it a privilege to have the opportunity to honor a man he held in the highest regard. So Fitz used the famous work ethic he was known for as a player on that speech. He used the same attention to detail that got him to Canton today. Back in 2018 it was an early morning at the Cardinals practice facility and I was doing hits for NFL Network. I was the only person in the media workroom. Larry walked into the room in a suit, he said hello, and he went into a back room. He didn’t come back out for hours. Later that day I asked around about what Larry was doing. I was told he was practicing. He was wearing the suit he was going to wear at the service. He was standing at a podium in that room to simulate the setting for his speech to honor his friend. He cared so much that he wouldn’t quit until he felt it was perfect. And when he took that stage he was. Just as he was today with his speech in Canton. Some people are just wired a certain way. With a work ethic and drive to be great in everything they do. It’s why Larry Fitzgerald is a Hall of Fame football player and Hall of Fame person.

title: Looks like the Giants dodged their first major injury scare of camp. Greg Newsome, who has been their most consistent corner, went down with an apparent non-contact knee injury. He hobbled off and was checked by trainers with GM Joe Schoen joining in. But Newsome apparently checked out OK. He popped up, put his helmet back on and rejoined his teammates on the sideline. He didn’t participate in the rest of practice, but still looks like the Giants avoided anything serious.

title: The Giants just concluded their final West Virginia practice. In pads with some real team work, but also kept goal line mostly jog thru and ended a bit early 3rd team O & D finished with a live goal line period Brian Burns (ankle) had a great day. 2 sacks in team period and strong in 1-on-1s Cam Skattebo took a couple real 9-on-7 carries, which is encouraging after being banged up yesterday, but didn’t do 11-on-11 Corner Greg Newsome looked like he had a left knee scare when his foot got caught in the grass, but he seemed to avoid anything serious Top center JMS (head injury) did not practice. Lucas Patrick stayed out of teamwork. So Bryan Hudson & Jake Kubas manned center. Hudson did well, including in 1-on-1s Malik Nabers looked good in individuals again. DJ Reader got a vet day, and some vet reps like Andrew Thomas’ were managed Deonte Banks continues to mostly log snaps ahead of Paulson Adebo Kicking update: Ben Sauls 5 of 7. Dominic Zvada 6 of 6 including two BOMBS 💣 from 52 and 56 @NYDailyNews See you in NJ for Vikings game week!
